 Judgment

The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that occurred on 01-03-2024.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 01-03-2024 at about 4.30 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding on the Honda Activa bearing No. KA-04- JV-4302 from Marappannapalya, Ashokpuram road, near RJ Royal Hotel, Opp. Venkateshwara Garage,
at that time the driver of Tata Goods Eicher Canter bearing No.KA-02- AA-2625 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and hit the motor cycle of the petitioner from the back side.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Sparsh Super Speciality Hospital, Tumkur Road, Yeshwanthapur, Bengaluru wherein he was admitted as inpatient for 14 days and outpatient for last five months and injury suffered due to the accident are grievous in nature and caused permanent disability.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and aged about 36 years and he was working as Professional Advisor at Red Bricks Constructions,
Kadabugere, Bengaluru and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.

entities.text: Sparsh Super Speciality Hospital, Tumkur Road, Yeshwanthapur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue with his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the driver, respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-02- AA-2625 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of summons, respondent No.1 & 2 owner and driver of the offending vehicle appeared through their counsels, but failed to file written statements.

4. The following points arise for my consideration:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Tata Goods Eicher vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625 by its driver, in RTA took place on 01-03-2024 at about 4.30 p.m., on Ashokapuram road, near Venkateshwara Garage, Marapanna- Sanjay V vs Prabhakaran G on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187548752/
2 palya, Yeshwanthpur Industrial Area, Bengaluru?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, at what amount and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 16 and 20 to 23.
Petitioner also examined one witness as PW2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.17 to P.19.
In spite of sufficient opportunities the respondents have neither cross-examined the PW1 and 2 nor lead any evidence.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above points are as under.

Point No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Point No.2 : In the affirmative  Point No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as PW.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, police intimation, seizer mahazar,
IMV notice and reply, Seizure mahazar, wound certificate, IMV report, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 12.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR which is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by the petitioner himself.
The contents of Ex.P.1 & 2 are in consonance with the petition averments.
After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P3 spot mahazar and Ex.P4 rough sketch of the accident spot was prepared by the IO.

On perusal of the contents of Ex.P3 & 4 mahazar and rough sketch, the accident spot is in the left side portion of the road nad the driver of offending canter bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625 changed its lane towards the left side and caused the accident.
10. Further the Ex.P12 being the IMV report shows that the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625 has got no fresh visible damages.
On the other hand, the motorcycle of the petitioner has got damages in its right hand side body scratched, front wheel mudguard dent and scratched.

Thus, the contents of Ex.P3 & 4 mahazar and rough sketch along with the contents of Ex.P12 IMV report supported the case of the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Tata Goods Eicher vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625.

sentences.text: Ex.P20 charge sheet was also came to be filed on the driver and owner of the offending Tata Goods Eicher vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625 wherein, the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of Tata Goods Eicher vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625.

It is very important to note that the respondent No.1 being the driver and respondent No.2 being the owner of the Tata Goods Eicher vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625 not disputed the alleged negligence.
No doubt that the findings of the criminal court has no relevancy in the trial of claim petition.

But in this case the driver of Tata Goods Eicher vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625 appeared before the criminal court and pleaded guilty for the alleged offences and also paid the fine as per Ex.P21 to Ex.P.23.
12.

In the present petition, filed by seeking compensation, the respondent No.1 & 2 remained silent even after the appearance and thereby they have not chosen to file written statement or to lead rebuttal evidence to deny the case of the petitioner.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence on the part of petitioner.
13. As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of offending vehicle.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident was caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Tata Goods Eicher vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625.
14.
The charge sheet was came to be filed against the respondent No.1 who is the driver of the Tata Goods Eicher vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

Hence, by relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to23, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of Tata Goods Eicher vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625.
15.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

17. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 01-03-2024 which was caused by the driver of Tata Goods Eicher vehicle bearing No.KA- 02-AA-2625 which belonging to respondent No.2 and driven by respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
18.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which was caused by respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
19. The petitioner has produced wound certificate as per Ex.P11 which shows that the petitioner sustained right leg extreme degloving injury which is grievous in nature.
The discharge summary is not produced by the petitioner.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated him at the time of accident.
Without the evidence of doctor, it is not possible to believe that, the petitioner has sustained disability due to grievous injuries.

20. While determining the compensation this court has to looked into the pain and sufferings,
medical expenses, diet, food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges and loss of amenities and enjoyment of life that the PW-1 has suffered, which are discussed herein below:
(A) TOWARDS PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The petitioner has relied upon Ex.P.11- wound certificate which make it crystal clear that PW-1 has sustained grievous injury.

Hence keeping in mind the injuries mentioned in wound certificate, it can be said that the petitioner must have undergone some amount of physical pain and sufferings, for which, an amount of Rs.40,000/- can be held to be just and proper compensation under this head.
(B) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced bills which are marked as Ex.P-14.
In the said bills the advance receipts are also included, hence the said bills cannot be considered.
For the better appreciation of this point the details of the bills are hereby reproduced in table format.

In this case the above referred medical bills are not original bills and they are photo copies of the bills.

It is very important to note that the Sl.No.1, 3, 4 are the medicine purchase bills in which the payor is shown as Adithya Birla.
Further the bills referred above in Sl.No.5,7 and 9 which are the inpatient bill are mentioned as "IP tax invoice credit Provisional".
This shows that the petitioner not produced the final bill and the said bills are the provisional bills.
In the absence of production of the copies of final bill the bills cannot be reimbursed on the basis of provisional bills.

Thus, even though the said bills marked at Sl. No.5, 7 and 9 shows that only partial payment was made by sponsor Adithya Birla and partial amount was paid by the petitioner, the partial bills also cannot be reimbursed on the basis of provisional bills.
The petitioner also produced the advance receipts along with medical bills.
But as the petitioner failed to produce the final bill, the bills produced at Ex.P.14 being the provisional bills cannot be reimbursed.
The bills which are referred above in Sl. No.2,6 and 8 shows that the payment was made by the petitioner through cash and UPI.
The total amount of bills of Sl. No.2, 6 and 8 will be Rs.1,987/- and same is liable to be reimbursed.
By rounding off the said amount Rs.2,000/- is awarded under this head.
(C) TOWARDS DIET, FOOD, NOURISHMENT, ATTENDANT AND CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
As already observed the Ex.P-11 makes it amply clear that the petitioner underwent treatment for the injuries sustained by him.
The petitioner has produced wound certificate as per Ex.P11 which shows that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

On consideration of the injuries sustained by the petitioner this Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and proper to award an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
(D) TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNING CAPACITY ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
It is necessary to note that the loss of future earning capacity cannot be presumed and has to be proved with cogent evidence.
But interestingly the petitioner though claims that he is unable to do any work and has become disabled he has not put in any efforts to prove the disability by examining the doctor, who treated him.
In fact he has not even produced the disability certificate issued by competent authority.
In the absence of any such material piece of evidence, it is very difficult for this Court to assess the disability and thereby assess the loss of earning capacity due to disability.
This makes it clear that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability.

Further in the judgment reported in 2020(4) KCCR 2621 between Sri Nandish K. V/s United India Insurance Co. Ltd. & another wherein it is held that no compensation could be awarded towards the loss of earning capacity if physical disability do not effect claimant's capacity to work.

sentences.text: These answers given by the PW.1 evidentiates that the petitioner is continued in the service and no disability is caused which effects his earning capacity.

Hence, this court has no option but to hold that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability which has resulted in reduction of his salary and hence he is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
(E) TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
According to the petitioner he was working as Professional Advisor at Red Bricks Constructions, Bengaluru, and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.
To prove his avocation and income, the petitioner has not produced any documents.
But examined one Bharath as PW2 who deposed that the Ex.P.15 letter was issued by him as a proprietor and he was paying Rs.50,000/- as salary per month to the petitioner.
In support of the said letter and evidence of PW2, the PW2 not produced any attendance register or any ID card of the petitioner by showing that the petitioner was working with him.

In the absence of corroborative evidence to show that the petitioner was working under PW2, merely on the basis of the oral evidence of PW2 the Ex.P.15 cannot be accepted in the absence of the evidence the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- as the accident of the year 2024.
The discharge summary is not produced by the petitioner.
But the bills marked at Ex.P.14 shows that the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for considerable time.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total 5 months period including inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income as the petitioner Sanjay V vs Prabhakaran G on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187548752/
7 sustained only one cut injury.

sentences.text: So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,500 X 5 months = Rs.82,500/- during the laid up period.
F) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident and took treatment as an inpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.5,000/- is awarded in total towards attendant charges.
(G) TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES AND ENJOYMENT OF LIFE:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Admittedly the petitioner is continued with his earlier job.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award him a reasonable sum of Rs.35,000/- under this head.

LIABILITY:

21. As per the reasons discussed in Issue No.1 the petitioner has got injuries in the RTA dated 01.03.2024 which was caused by the actionable negligence of the driver of Tata Goods Eicher Canter vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625 and the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.
22.
The present petition is filed U/Sec.166 of IMV Act by claiming the compensation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are the driver and owner of the Tata Goods Eicher Canter vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625.

At the cost of repetition as per the reasons discussed in Issue No.1 the negligence of the driver of Tata Goods Eicher Canter vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625 is Sanjay V vs Prabhakaran G on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187548752/
8 established.
When the petition filed U/Sec.166 of IMV Act by claiming the compensation, the fact of negligence place very important role to fix the liability.
In this regard the petitioner successfully established the negligence of the driver of Tata Goods Eicher Canter vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA- 2625.

The Tata Goods Eicher Canter vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625 was not insured, as such the liability for the negligent act of the driver of Tata Goods Eicher Canter vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AA-2625 has to be fastened on the owner.

Accordingly, this issue answered partly in the affirmative ISSUE NO.3:
23.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petition against the respondent No.1 - driver stands dismissed.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.1,94,500/- (Rupees One lakh ninety four thousand five hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondent No.2.
The respondent No.2 - owner is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
